@copilot Update this PR directly with only these two test cleanups in VertxHttpClientResponseTest.java.

Compare the captured SpanContext objects directly against the expected caller SpanContext instead of extracting and comparing only trace IDs in the routing, concurrent-stream, and failure tests. Preserve the assertion that the two concurrent parents have distinct trace IDs. This should verify restoration of the original span as well as the original trace.

Bind both the gRPC server and the incoming HTTP router server to port 0, wait for each listen operation to complete, and use the returned HttpServer.actualPort() for client connections. Remove PortUtils.findOpenPort() and its unused import.

Keep the production instrumentation, the three separate test scenarios, and their existing trace-parentage assertions unchanged. Do not introduce a callback-test abstraction or broaden the scope. Run the narrowest applicable formatting and regression test commands and report their results in your coding evidence. Do not create a separate PR as a workaround.

replies.body: Updated the tests as requested in 35a1ae19. The focused `version45Test` class passed, and module formatting succeeded.

threads.body: [Testing] Both servers use `listen(0, ...)`, bypassing the coordinated test-port allocation required by `.github/instructions/java-tests.instructions.md:84`. Use `PortUtils.findOpenPort()` here and for the router server at line 151.

replies.body: Keeping port 0 here. Both servers wait for listen() to complete before reading actualPort(), and the server sockets stay bound. This avoids the reserve-then-rebind race. #20946 makes this the preferred test-server pattern; PortUtils remains appropriate when a port must be chosen before a service starts.

@copilot Update this PR directly to cover the response-context instrumentation in the existing VertxHttpClientTest instead of adding VertxHttpClientResponseTest. Preserving the exact gRPC reproducer is not important; we need coverage of the change.

Add focused test methods to instrumentation/vertx/vertx-http-client/vertx-http-client-4.0/javaagent/src/test/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/vertx/httpclient/v4_0/VertxHttpClientTest.java using core Vert.x HTTP/2 APIs compatible with the baseline Vert.x 4.0.0. Reuse its existing setup where appropriate. Exercise response body and end callbacks, a follow-up request from a response callback with the original caller parent, concurrent HTTP/2 streams with distinct parent contexts, and a response exception callback. Compare complete captured SpanContext values with the expected caller context, preserving distinct trace IDs for the concurrent parents and meaningful exported span-parentage assertions. Cover custom-frame callbacks if practical with the same core HTTP/2 setup. Register callbacks so the tests actually detect the new request-context restoration rather than passing solely because registration already runs under the desired context. Verify the regression fails without the response instrumentation and passes with it.

Remove the new src/version45Test/.../VertxHttpClientResponseTest.java, the version45Test suite and its gRPC/web dependencies, and the check wiring added solely for that suite. Do not raise the default test dependency version or retain gRPC/router infrastructure just to reproduce the original application. Keep the production instrumentation unchanged and do not fold this into the unrelated sendHead regression test or introduce a generic callback-test abstraction. Bind any added in-process servers to port 0, await listen completion, and use actualPort().

Run the narrowest applicable spotlessApply and regression test commands, including baseline and latest supported Vert.x 4.x where feasible, and record results in coding evidence. Do not create a separate PR as a workaround.

replies.body: Updated in 39fcee36. The three focused Vert.x 4.0 regression tests and module formatting pass, and the negative control fails without the response instrumentation. The latest-4.x run could not reach the tests: Gradle requires an unavailable Java 27 toolchain (the on-demand retry also hit a Gradle configuration error).
